hidden_data_integrity: Declared overlap: the final is IFEval rows ordered[128:541] (413 rows) by sha256(key). The proxy is ordered[128:256], a 128-row prefix of the final (grade.py:23-26,76-79,193-211), mounted in explore (declaration.py:87-89). So 31.0% of the scored set is visible during exploration. This is stated to agents (instruction.md:81). final_eval.py:138-173 reports score(P), score(F\P) and the gap as diagnostics only (final_eval.py:17-19). The 128 retired rows ordered[:128] are scored by neither tier.

The 285 held-out rows are mounted only in the score phase (declaration.py:10-14,176-186; assets.lock.yaml:108-137). Retrain mounts no IFEval at all (declaration.py:102-115). The split rule is readable in grade.py, but the held-out text is not. Case pages (e.g. Sonnet low, Luna medium, Sol max, Terra xhigh) report literal searches for the 285 held-out prompts/keys in trajectories and patches with zero matches.

The final data is the public google/IFEval@966cd895 (task.toml:47). Agent LLMs can recall its 25 instruction families, and the lighteval IFEval checkers ship in the image for fast_eval (grade.py:258-319). network_mode = no-network (task.toml:32) blocks download. The two top cells (Opus high/medium) built synthetic constraint-pair data for those families from UltraFeedback; this is allowed by instruction.md:83 but specialises to the benchmark. Opus high's held-out complement score 173/285 = 0.607 shows the gain is not proxy memorisation.

Training on the 128 visible proxy prompts is not explicitly forbidden (instruction.md:83 bans only held-out prompts). The proxy is not mounted in retrain, so it would have to ride in the patch. inspect_patch (orchestrator/runner.py:185-237) screens for data files but not Python literals. No case page reports this happening.
scorer_issues: The scorer matches the instruction: prompt-level strict accuracy on 413 rows, greedy, chat template, max_new_tokens 1280 (grade.py:93-99,336-388; generate.py:46,56; final_eval.py:245-289). There are no gates to check.

MINOR: lighteval IFEval is patched (frozen regex sentence/word tokenizers replace nltk; non-alphabetic letter_frequency rows accepted; grade.py:102-128,258-319). Numbers are therefore not exactly official-IFEval comparable but are consistent within the benchmark.

Format/length gaming: no universal hack, because IFEval constraints conflict across rows (lowercase vs capital, no-comma vs lists). Length_clipped is reported (grade.py:386-387). No case shows format collapse. The realistic lever is teaching the constraint families (Opus high/medium), which is a construct caveat, not a scorer bug.
Reported-result inconsistency (one cell): codex Sol xhigh's credited best 0.4818 comes from an orphan summary that the page itself says is 'official result not available'.
anchor_issues: The paper baseline 0.424 (scripts/score.py:21) matches neither of the case pages' references: fixed start 0.3971 (164/413) and shipped recipe 0.5085 (210/413, instruction.md:93-95). However, four formal replays of the unchanged current recipe in the case pages score 0.39-0.44: Sol none 165/413, and Terra xhigh branches at 161, 167 and 181/413. Their mean, 0.408, is close to the paper's 0.424. So the paper anchor is plausible, and the instruction's 210/413 shipped reference, which agents were shown, is not reproduced. A likely cause is stale configuration: declaration.py:19,84 say the shipped default reads 8,192 rows, while solution/run.sh:33 uses 61,135. Had sigma been anchored on 0.5085, task mean sigma would fall from 0.187 to 0.116 and cells above 0.1 from 22 to 7.
Uninformative 0 and optimum 1 are sensible for strict accuracy. Sigma=1 needs 413/413, which is not reachable without solving the task.
task_level.noise: n=413, binomial SE about 0.024, so two cells' unpaired difference has SE about 0.034. Seed variance is visible in the pages. Same-seed replicates of the shipped recipe differ by 6 items (Terra xhigh branches 10/11: 161 vs 167), and a seed change adds up to 20 items (181). The shipped-recipe reference differs from replays by about 42 items. Only Opus medium/high (0.622/0.615) separate clearly from the 0.40-0.56 pack. Orderings among the 0.43-0.50 cells (about 15 cells) are within noise, and so is beat/miss of the 0.424 baseline for cells between 0.40 and 0.47.
task_level.checkpoint_selection: In 16 of 29 cells the reported checkpoint is not the last one. Task mean sigma is 0.1868 with best-of-3 vs 0.1734 with the last checkpoint; the mean raw gain is about 0.014 (about 6 items of 413), selected on the scored set. One cell flips across sigma=0.1 (Opus low 0.4673 vs 0.4092). Terra xhigh turns best-of-3 into a seed lottery over three independent shipped-recipe replicates.

task_level.summary: MINOR, confirmed, not counted. The held-out 285 IFEval rows are not exposed (score-only mount; no matches in trajectories per case pages). The 31% proxy overlap is declared and diagnosed by score(F\P). The scorer matches the instruction. Caveats: (1) the instruction's shipped reference 210/413, repeated on every case page, is not reproduced by four formal replays of the unchanged recipe (161-181/413), likely due to stale 8,192-row config; the paper anchor 0.424 is actually consistent with the replays. (2) The two top cells win by synthesising IFEval-family constraint pairs, which is legitimate under the rules but teaches to the test; it does generalise to the held-out complement (0.607). (3) Most inter-configuration gaps are inside binomial plus seed noise. (4) One cell exploits best-of-3 with seed replicates (Terra xhigh, FP) and one credits an orphan summary (Sol xhigh, unclear).
